title: Pods hold containers
summary: A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest runnable unit. Containers in one Pod share some resources, such as the network address.
introduction: A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest runnable unit. Containers in one Pod share some resources, such as the network address. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest runnable unit. Containers in one Pod share some resources, such as the network address.

blocks.code:
Pod: club-web
Container: web server
Pod network address: shared by containers in that Pod
blocks.title: Pods hold containers

blocks.text: Most simple examples put one main container in a Pod. A Pod is not a whole virtual machine.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw two Pods, each containing one web container.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not expect an individual Pod name or address to last forever.
For more detail later, use this [Kubernetes further reading](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/kubernetes-basics/).
